Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) Psychology – Psychological and Brain Sciences
Program Requirements:
A minimum of 60 credit hours are required for the degree program. A maximum of 30 hours credit may be transferred.
• Involves course work on the biological basis of behavior and scientific inquiry.
• It also has an apprenticeship model in which each student works closely and continuously with a faculty member
within the realm of the faculty member's research interests. This work will result in an empirical research thesis
and an empirical research dissertation.
Degree Completion Requirements:
• Qualifying Examination: After completion of two years in the program, students must pass written and oral
exams to continue in the program. Students are also required to complete a specialty paper for publication.
• Dissertation: All students must defend orally a written dissertation proposal to their dissertation committee. A
dissertation embodying the results of original research must be accepted by the faculty and the Graduate
School.
Application Requirements:
1. Online Graduate Application
2. Statement of Purpose: Please submit a sentence or two about what you plan to do (e.g., I plan to earn a Ph.D.
degree…)
3. Official transcripts from all universities attended. A Bachelor’s degree is required.
4. Entrance examinations:
a. International Students must document English proficiency by providing scores from an internationally
accepted standardized examination. See International Admissions for more information.
5. Minimum GPA of 3.0 on 4.0 scale overall and 3.2 in Psychology courses
6. Letters of Recommendation: 3 letters of recommendation are required from individuals who are familiar with
the applicant's potential to successfully complete graduate training in biological psychology. Ideally, individuals
who provide letters of recommendation will be sufficiently familiar with the candidate to address critical
thinking, academic success, written and oral expression, responsibility, organization, and other important skills
necessary for successful graduate training.
7. Personal Statement: Please submit a statement of 300-400 words with your rationale for seeking admission to
the Ph.D. program in Psychological and Brain Sciences. Describe your interest in the biological basis of behavior,
any prior research experience, your career goals, and which faculty member(s) you would like to work with and
why.
8. Submit a current professional resume/CV: Please submit a CV with information about your higher education
(school name, degree, major/minor/emphasis area, (expected) graduation month and year, and grade point
average), any research experience, relevant work experience, any software skills.
9. Other: Any information that the student feels is pertinent (e.g. writing sample) may be submitted directly to the
Program Director Dr. Carissa Philippi.
Application Deadlines:
Fall Semester Only - The deadline for receipt of all admission materials is December 1 of each year for admission
Application Fees:
$50 for domestic applicants
$40 for international applicants
Assistantships:
Students in the Ph.D. program receive a Graduate Teaching Assistantship ($21,000/year + including tuition remission) in
their first and second year. Funding in later years is not guaranteed but could come from grant funding and/or teaching
courses.
